scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Executive summary

You're measured on cutting the $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit that opens in six months. Those two facts, not the migration itself, are what should decide whether this programme moves forward. The current estate — 28 Microsoft SQL Server instances on 620 Hyper-V virtual machines — carries the licensing, hardware refresh, and administrative overhead that make up that run-rate figure. [PF-2.4 GAP: the portion of the $1,850,000 attributable specifically to the SQL Server/Hyper-V footprint versus other technology spend was not supplied]. The proposed programme moves load-matching and carrier-settlement off that estate onto Google Compute Engine and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL over 24 months at a cost of $4,200,000. [PF-2.4 GAP: no projected post-migration run-rate or payback-period figure was supplied, so a return-on-investment claim cannot be stated here].

You should expect the programme to run through discovery, migration waves, and cutover on a 24-month schedule you and the team review at each phase, with the audit timeline treated as a hard constraint on any work touching carrier-settlement data. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm before this ships whether the vendor can commit to sequencing settlement-system changes so no migration work is in flight during the six-month DOT audit window]. [PF-2.4 GAP: no evidence was supplied for how Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL's compliance posture supports a clean DOT audit outcome specifically]. Before this moves forward, name the SQL Server/Hyper-V cost baseline and the audit's specific data and system requirements — those two inputs are what will let the next version of this summary state, rather than gap-mark, the business case you're accountable for.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| GAP | PF-2.4 | Portion of $1,850,000 attributable to the SQL Server/Hyper-V estate |
| GAP | PF-2.4 | Projected post-migration run-rate or payback period for the $4,200,000 programme |
| REVIEW (commitment) | PF-2.14 | Confirm whether sequencing can guarantee no settlement-system migration work occurs during the 6-month DOT audit window |
| GAP | PF-2.4 | Evidence that Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL supports a clean DOT compliance audit outcome |
